Use the model above to determine the missing number in the equation below.

$$
\frac{4}{5}÷\frac{9}{10}=\frac{\boxed{\,\,}}{9}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The denominators are $5$ and $10.$ We can make a common denominator of $10$ by splitting the shape on the left into $2$ parts vertically: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14153326/assets/9792dd036c4de182d4cd491830bbca85d083b7b19e80c356e67615d8f00db230.png)

 

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{8}{10}÷\frac{9}{10}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
8÷9=\frac{8}{9}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{4}{5}÷\frac{9}{10}=\frac{\boxed{\,8\,}}{9}\,.
$$

Therefore, the missing number is $8.$
